stories.title: Signing in
stories.description: A shopper signs in as a Swag Labs user, stays signed in, and signs out. Also owns the shop's server and the page shell every signed-in page uses.

capabilities.title: 1 · Shop server
capabilities.description: The node:http server behind npm start: serves on PORT (default 3000), finds every story package and serves the pages and browser files each one registers, and answers 404 for anything else.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Serves on PORT, 3000 by default
contracts.description: npm start listens on the PORT setting, or 3000 when none is given.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Story packages plug themselves in
contracts.description: Every workspace package exporting register(shop) is loaded at start, and the pages and browser files it registers are served.

contracts.title: 1.3 · Unknown addresses get 404
contracts.description: Any address no story registered answers 404, and asset paths cannot escape their package folder.

contracts.title: 1.4 · npm run reset empties the data folder
contracts.description: npm run reset deletes every .json file in SHOP_DATA_DIR (or <repo root>/data), leaving other files alone, so the shop starts again from its starting data.

contracts.title: 1.5 · Exact routes come before asset files
contracts.description: A route registered for an /assets/ address answers instead of the file, so a story can serve a live version of another story's browser module; a page may answer { redirect } to send the browser elsewhere.

capabilities.title: 2 · Session
capabilities.description: Being signed in and out: the session-username cookie, the guard that sends signed-out browsers to the sign-in page, and /logout that clears the cookie.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Signed-out browsers are sent to the sign-in page
contracts.description: Any signed-in page asked for without a session-username cookie redirects to /.

contracts.title: 2.2 · A session-username cookie counts as signed in
contracts.description: A browser holding a non-empty session-username cookie (as set by document.cookie in the e2e tests) gets signed-in pages.

contracts.title: 2.3 · Signing out clears the cookie
contracts.description: GET /logout expires session-username (Path=/) and redirects to /.

capabilities.title: 3 · Sign-in page
capabilities.description: The page at / with #login_button_container, #user-name, #password and the .btn_action button; signs standard_user in, and shows the Epic sadface errors in [data-test=\"error\"].

contracts.title: 3.1 · The sign-in form is at /
contracts.description: GET / shows #login_button_container holding #user-name, #password and a .btn_action button, even to a signed-in browser.

reported.note: Also passes Swag Labs' login.spec 'loading of login page' in Edge.

contracts.title: 3.2 · standard_user signs in to Products
contracts.description: standard_user / secret_sauce sets session-username=standard_user and redirects to /inventory.html.

reported.note: Also passes Swag Labs' login.spec 'login with a standard user' in Edge.

contracts.title: 3.3 · locked_out_user is refused
contracts.description: Shows [data-test=\"error\"] \"Epic sadface: Sorry, this user has been locked out.\" and sets no cookie.

reported.note: Also passes Swag Labs' login.spec 'locked user' in Edge.

contracts.title: 3.4 · Missing or wrong details show their error
contracts.description: \"Epic sadface: Username is required\", then \"Epic sadface: Password is required\", then \"Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service\", in [data-test=\"error\"], with no cookie set.

contracts.title: 3.5 · Errors show at once, without loading a new page
contracts.description: On Login with missing details, or a Swag Labs username with a wrong password or locked out, the page's script cancels the submit and draws [data-test=\"error\"] in place during the click, as saucedemo.com does (login.spec checks it without waiting). Good details, and usernames only another story's accounts can judge (part 5), go on to the server.

contracts.title: 3.6 · Other stories' accounts can sign in
contracts.description: signing-in exports a seam for registering account sources; the sign-in POST accepts an account a source vouches for, after the Swag Labs users. Built in part 5.

capabilities.title: 4 · Page shell
capabilities.description: The frame of every signed-in page: the Swag Labs header with the .shopping_cart_link to /cart.html (empty when the cart is empty), the title, and the hook other stories use to add header pieces and scripts.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Signed-in pages have the header with an empty cart link
contracts.description: Every page drawn in the shell has a .shopping_cart_link to /cart.html with no text in it.

contracts.title: 4.2 · Other stories can add to the header
contracts.description: HTML and scripts given to shop.addToHeader appear in the header of every signed-in page.

contracts.title: 4.3 · Header pieces can depend on who is signed in
contracts.description: A header piece's html may be a function of the request's ctx (with username); pieces given as plain html keep working. Built in part 5; the Admin link uses it in part 9.

stories.title: Browsing
stories.description: A shopper looks through the six products, sorts them, opens a product's page, and adds or removes products from the cart, seeing the count in the header badge.

capabilities.title: 1 · Product catalog
capabilities.description: The six Swag Labs products with ids 0 to 5, names, saucedemo.com descriptions and prices, as one ES module the server and browsers both import.

contracts.title: 1.1 · The six products with their ids and prices
contracts.description: Ids 0 to 5: Bike Light $9.99, Bolt T-Shirt $15.99, Onesie $7.99, Test.allTheThings() T-Shirt (Red) $15.99, Backpack $29.99, Fleece Jacket $49.99, each with its saucedemo.com description.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Browsers can load the catalog
contracts.description: /assets/browsing/catalog/products.js is served as a JavaScript module.

contracts.title: 1.3 · Browsers get the current prices
contracts.description: /assets/browsing/catalog/products.js is still a JavaScript module with the same exports, carrying the current prices (not cached), so the cart, overview and sorting use them. Built in part 9.

capabilities.title: 2 · Products page
capabilities.description: /inventory.html: .inventory_list with one .inventory_item per product, each with .inventory_item_name linking to its product page, .inventory_item_desc, .inventory_item_price and an Add to cart button, listed by name A to Z.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Lists all six products A to Z
contracts.description: /inventory.html has .inventory_list with six .inventory_item, ordered by name A to Z (Backpack first).

reported.note: Also passes Swag Labs' swag.items.list.spec 'all products are present' in Edge.

contracts.title: 2.2 · Each item shows name, description, price and Add to cart
contracts.description: .inventory_item_name links to /inventory-item.html?id=<id>, .inventory_item_desc, .inventory_item_price like \"$29.99\", and an Add to cart button with classes btn_primary btn_inventory.

contracts.title: 2.3 · Other stories can add to each item
contracts.description: HTML that other stories register for a product appears inside that product's .inventory_item. Built in part 9; reviews uses it in part 8.

capabilities.title: 3 · Cart store
capabilities.description: The browser module that reads and writes localStorage 'cart-contents' (a JSON array of product ids): ids, has, add, remove, clear, count, and a 'cart-change' event on every change. The seam browsing, the cart and checkout all use.

contracts.title: 3.1 · Reads cart-contents as a list of ids
contracts.description: ids() returns the JSON array in localStorage 'cart-contents' (e.g. [4]); missing or broken contents read as an empty cart.

contracts.title: 3.2 · Add, remove and clear write cart-contents back
contracts.description: add(id) (no duplicates), remove(id) and clear() store the new array in 'cart-contents'; count() and has(id) follow.

contracts.title: 3.3 · Every change announces cart-change
contracts.description: add, remove and clear dispatch a 'cart-change' event on window carrying the new ids.

capabilities.title: 4 · Product page
capabilities.description: /inventory-item.html?id=<id>: .inventory_details with .inventory_details_name, .inventory_details_desc, .inventory_details_price and .inventory_details_back_button back to Products.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Shows the product named in the address
contracts.description: /inventory-item.html?id=<id> has .inventory_details with that product's .inventory_details_name, .inventory_details_desc and .inventory_details_price.

reported.note: npm test 34/34. Swag Labs swag.item.details 3/3 in Edge, 4 runs.

contracts.title: 4.2 · Back to Products
contracts.description: .inventory_details_back_button goes to /inventory.html.

reported.note: Also passes swag.item.details 'go back from the details' in Edge, 4 runs.

contracts.title: 4.3 · Opened from the product's name
contracts.description: Clicking an .inventory_item_name on Products opens that product's page.

reported.note: Also passes swag.items.list 'details of a product can be opened' in Edge, 4 runs.

contracts.title: 4.4 · Other stories can add under the product
contracts.description: HTML that other stories register for a product appears on its product page under the product. Built in part 9; reviews uses it in part 8.

capabilities.title: 5 · Sorting
capabilities.description: The .product_sort_container menu on Products: name A to Z (default), name Z to A, price low to high, price high to low.

contracts.title: 5.1 · Sort menu with four orders
contracts.description: .product_sort_container offers name A to Z (selected by default), name Z to A, price low to high, price high to low.

contracts.title: 5.2 · Choosing an order reorders the list
contracts.description: Each choice reorders the .inventory_item elements at once, keeping their buttons.

reported.note: Also checked in real Edge with a throwaway wdio spec (not committed): hilo/lohi/za orders, active label, Remove button kept.

capabilities.title: 6 · Cart buttons and badge
capabilities.description: Add to cart (btn_primary btn_inventory) / Remove (btn_secondary btn_inventory) on the Products and product pages, and the badge inside .shopping_cart_link showing the count, empty when the cart is.

contracts.title: 6.1 · Add to cart becomes Remove
contracts.description: On Products and the product page, Add to cart (btn_primary btn_inventory) adds the product and turns into Remove (btn_secondary btn_inventory); Remove does the reverse. Products already in cart-contents load as Remove.

reported.note: Also passes the add/remove tests of swag.items.list and swag.item.details in Edge, 4 runs.

contracts.title: 6.2 · The badge shows the count
contracts.description: On every signed-in page the .shopping_cart_link holds a badge with the number of products (\"1\") and no text at all when the cart is empty, following every cart-change.

reported.note: Badge is a header piece, so part 3/4 pages get it too. Swag Labs getCartAmount checks pass in Edge, 4 runs.

capabilities.title: 7 · Search
capabilities.description: [data-test=\"search\"] on Products filters as you type over names and descriptions, ignoring case; the address keeps it (/inventory.html?q=backpack); no match shows [data-test=\"no-results\"] and no .inventory_item; sorting works on the filtered list.

contracts.title: 7.1 · Typing filters the list
contracts.description: [data-test=\"search\"] on Products leaves only the .inventory_item whose name or description contains what is typed, ignoring case, as each key is typed.

contracts.title: 7.2 · The address keeps the search
contracts.description: Typing updates the address to /inventory.html?q=<text>; opening or reloading that address shows the same search and list.

contracts.title: 7.3 · No match says so
contracts.description: No match shows [data-test=\"no-results\"] \"No products match “<what was typed>”.\" and no .inventory_item.

contracts.title: 7.4 · Sorting works on the filtered list
contracts.description: With a search in place, az, za, lohi and hilo order the remaining items, and items brought back by changing the search take the chosen order.

stories.title: The cart
stories.description: A shopper reviews what is in the cart, removes products, goes back to shopping or on to checkout, and uses the side menu (All Items, About, Logout, Reset App State).

capabilities.title: 1 · Cart page
capabilities.description: /cart.html: #cart_contents_container with a .cart_item (name, description, price) per product in the cart, each with Remove (btn_secondary cart_button); Continue Shopping (btn_secondary) back to Products and Checkout (checkout_button) to /checkout-step-one.html.

contracts.title: 1.1 · One cart_item per product in the cart
contracts.description: /cart.html has #cart_contents_container with a .cart_item (name, description, price) for each id in cart-contents.

reported.note: npm test 30/30. Edge: cart items drawn from cart-contents.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Remove takes a product out
contracts.description: Remove (btn_secondary cart_button) removes the .cart_item and the product from the cart, and the badge follows.

reported.note: With part 2's badge merged: Swag Labs cart.summary.spec 'product can be removed' passes in Edge (badge 1, then empty). PR #5.

contracts.title: 1.3 · Continue Shopping and Checkout
contracts.description: Continue Shopping (btn_secondary) goes to /inventory.html; Checkout (checkout_button) goes to /checkout-step-one.html; the header's cart link opens this page.

reported.note: With part 4 merged: cart.summary.spec 3/3 in Edge, including 'cart to checkout'. PR #5.

capabilities.title: 2 · Menu
capabilities.description: The .bm-burger-button on every signed-in page opening a side menu: All Items (#inventory_sidebar_link), About (#about_sidebar_link to https://saucelabs.com/), Logout (#logout_sidebar_link to /logout) and Reset App State (#reset_sidebar_link, clears the cart and the badge at once).

contracts.title: 2.1 · The burger button opens the menu
contracts.description: Every signed-in page has .bm-burger-button; clicking it shows the side menu with its four links.

reported.note: Edge: menu.spec opens the menu from /cart.html.

contracts.title: 2.2 · All Items, About and Logout go where they should
contracts.description: #inventory_sidebar_link to /inventory.html, #about_sidebar_link to https://saucelabs.com/, #logout_sidebar_link signs out to the sign-in page.

reported.note: Swag Labs menu.spec All Items, About, Logout pass in Edge.

contracts.title: 2.3 · Reset App State empties the cart at once
contracts.description: #reset_sidebar_link clears cart-contents and the badge straight away, without a reload.

reported.note: With parts 2 and 4 merged: npm test 51/51, including '2.3 on every signed-in page, Reset App State empties the badge at once' (proven able to fail). Edge: Swag Labs menu.spec 4/4, and the badge is empty right after Reset on all six signed-in pages. PR #5.

contracts.title: 2.4 · Other stories can add links to the menu
contracts.description: Links registered by other stories appear in the side menu after the Swag Labs links, each shown only to the users its rule allows. Built in part 6.

reported.note: when(ctx) rules are honoured by renderMenu(ctx); the header still draws the menu without ctx until part 5's ctx-aware header pieces land, so rule-bound links stay hidden until then (part 9b wires it).

stories.title: Checkout
stories.description: A shopper gives their name and postal code, reviews the order with its item total, 8% tax and total, finishes, and sees the order complete.

capabilities.title: 1 · Your information
capabilities.description: /checkout-step-one.html: #checkout_info_container with firstName, lastName and postalCode fields, Continue (cart_button) and Cancel (cart_cancel_link, back to the Cart); missing fields show the Error: ... is required messages in that order.

contracts.title: 1.1 · The information form
contracts.description: /checkout-step-one.html has #checkout_info_container with [data-test=\"firstName\"], [data-test=\"lastName\"], [data-test=\"postalCode\"], Continue (cart_button) and Cancel (cart_cancel_link) back to /cart.html.

reported.note: npm test 30/30. Edge: checkout.personal.info 2/3; 'cancel the first checkout' fails only because /cart.html is Part 3, not landed yet.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Missing fields show their error in order
contracts.description: \"Error: First Name is required\", then \"Error: Last Name is required\", then \"Error: Postal Code is required\" in [data-test=\"error\"]; all filled goes on to /checkout-step-two.html.

reported.note: Checked in the browser during the Continue click (no page load); good details go on to /checkout-step-two.html. Edge: the Postal Code error and continue specs pass.

contracts.title: 1.3 · Continue sends the details to the server for the order
contracts.description: Complete details are sent to POST /api/checkout-details before the overview opens; if the server cannot be reached the overview still opens, since an order may have no details. Built in part 6.

capabilities.title: 2 · Overview
capabilities.description: /checkout-step-two.html: #checkout_summary_container with a .cart_item per product (.inventory_item_name, .inventory_item_desc, .inventory_item_price), the item total, tax at 8% and the total; Finish (cart_button) and Cancel (cart_cancel_link, back to Products).

contracts.title: 2.1 · One cart_item per product, with name, description and price
contracts.description: /checkout-step-two.html has #checkout_summary_container with a .cart_item per id in cart-contents, each with .inventory_item_name, .inventory_item_desc and .inventory_item_price.

reported.note: Rows drawn in the browser from cart-contents. Edge: checkout.summary '1 product in our checkout overview' passes.

contracts.title: 2.2 · Item total, 8% tax and total
contracts.description: Shows the item total, tax at 8% and the total, worked in cents (Backpack: $29.99, $2.40, $32.39).

contracts.title: 2.3 · Finish and Cancel
contracts.description: Finish (cart_button) goes on to /checkout-complete.html; Cancel (cart_cancel_link) goes back to /inventory.html.

reported.note: Edge: checkout.summary finish and cancel specs pass.

capabilities.title: 3 · Order complete
capabilities.description: Finish empties the cart and shows /checkout-complete.html: #checkout_complete_container with .complete-header \"Thank you for your order!\" and a Back Home button to Products.

contracts.title: 3.1 · Finishing places the order, then empties the cart
contracts.description: Finish sends the cart's ids to POST /api/orders, and only once the server has the order does it empty the cart (the badge hears it) and go on to the complete page. If the server cannot be reached the cart is kept and the page stays. Changed in part 6.

contracts.title: 3.2 · Thank you for your order, and Back Home
contracts.description: /checkout-complete.html has #checkout_complete_container with .complete-header \"Thank you for your order!\" and a Back Home button to /inventory.html.

reported.note: Edge: checkout.complete 1/1.

stories.title: Accounts
stories.description: Anyone can sign up with a full name, username and password, then sign in and out like a Swag Labs user; every signed-in page greets them by name. Package packages/accounts.

capabilities.title: 1 · Account store
capabilities.description: The signed-up accounts (username, full name, hashed password) in a data file that survives a restart; knows which usernames are taken, including the Swag Labs ones.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Accounts survive a restart
contracts.description: An account signed up before the server restarts can still sign in after it.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Passwords are kept hashed
contracts.description: The accounts file never contains a password as typed.

capabilities.title: 2 · Sign-up page
capabilities.description: The Sign up link on the sign-in page ([data-test=\"signup-link\"]) and /signup.html with signup-name, signup-username, signup-password and signup-submit; the four rules in [data-test=\"error\"] in order; signing up signs in and goes to Products.

contracts.title: 2.1 · Sign up link and form
contracts.description: [data-test=\"signup-link\"] on the sign-in page goes to /signup.html, which has signup-name, signup-username, signup-password and signup-submit and is open to signed-out browsers.

contracts.title: 2.2 · Broken rules show their error in order
contracts.description: \"Error: Name is required\", then \"Error: Username is required\", then \"Error: Password must be at least 8 characters\", then \"Error: That username is taken\" (Swag Labs users count as taken) in [data-test=\"error\"]; nothing is saved.

contracts.title: 2.3 · Signing up signs in to Products
contracts.description: Good details save the account, set session-username to the new username and go to /inventory.html.

capabilities.title: 3 · Signing in with an account
capabilities.description: A signed-up user signs in on the sign-in page with their own password and signs out as before; wrong details show the Swag Labs mismatch error.

contracts.title: 3.1 · A signed-up user signs in again
contracts.description: After signing out, the new user signs in on the sign-in page with their password and reaches Products.

contracts.title: 3.2 · A wrong password is refused with the Swag Labs error
contracts.description: A signed-up username with a wrong password shows \"Epic sadface: Username and password do not match any user in this service\" and sets no cookie; Swag Labs' login.spec still passes.

reported.note: Passed before the store existed too (no accounts at all); it proves something only alongside 3.1, which was red first.

capabilities.title: 4 · Who is signed in
capabilities.description: [data-test=\"greeting\"] \"Hi, <full name>\" in the header of every signed-in page (the username for Swag Labs users), GET /api/me, and displayName(username) for other stories.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Every signed-in page greets the user
contracts.description: The header of every signed-in page has [data-test=\"greeting\"] \"Hi, <full name>\"; for Swag Labs users, \"Hi, <username>\".

contracts.title: 4.2 · GET /api/me answers who is signed in
contracts.description: {\"username\": ..., \"name\": ...} as JSON for a signed-in browser, 401 when nobody is signed in.

stories.title: Orders
stories.description: Finish saves the order on the server, numbered from 1001; a shopper sees their past orders under My Orders and opens each one. Package packages/orders.

capabilities.title: 1 · Order store
capabilities.description: Every order (number, username, products with their prices then, item total, tax, total, name, postal code, placed time) in a data file that survives a restart; numbers count up from 1001 across the shop. Exports ordersOf(username), orderFor(username, number) and hasOrdered(username, productId).

contracts.title: 1.1 · Orders survive a restart
contracts.description: Orders placed before a restart are still listed after it, and numbering carries on from where it stopped.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Numbers count up from 1001 across the shop
contracts.description: The shop's first order is 1001 and each next order, whoever places it, gets the next number.

capabilities.title: 2 · Placing an order
capabilities.description: Continue on checkout's first step hands the name and postal code to the server; Finish posts the cart's ids, the server saves the order and answers its number; the complete page shows [data-test=\"order-number\"] \"Order #1001\".

contracts.title: 2.1 · Finish saves the order for the signed-in user
contracts.description: The saved order has its products with their prices then, item total, 8% tax and total (worked out on the server), the name and postal code given at step one, and when it was placed. Finish still completes when step one was skipped.

contracts.title: 2.2 · The complete page shows the order number
contracts.description: /checkout-complete.html shows [data-test=\"order-number\"] \"Order #1001\" for the order just placed, alongside \"Thank you for your order!\"; Swag Labs' checkout specs still pass.

capabilities.title: 3 · My Orders page
capabilities.description: #orders_sidebar_link in the side menu to /orders.html: one [data-test=\"order-row\"] per order of this user, newest first, with number, date, item count and total, linking to /order.html?id=<number>; [data-test=\"no-orders\"] \"You haven't ordered anything yet.\" when there are none.

contracts.title: 3.1 · My Orders link in the side menu
contracts.description: #orders_sidebar_link in the side menu of every signed-in page goes to /orders.html.

contracts.title: 3.2 · One row per order of this user, newest first
contracts.description: Each [data-test=\"order-row\"] shows its number, date, item count and total and links to /order.html?id=<number>; other users' orders are not listed.

contracts.title: 3.3 · No orders yet
contracts.description: With no orders, /orders.html shows [data-test=\"no-orders\"] \"You haven't ordered anything yet.\" and no order-row.

capabilities.title: 4 · Order page
capabilities.description: /order.html?id=<number>: a .cart_item per product (.inventory_item_name, .inventory_item_price at the price then) and [data-test=\"order-total\"] \"Total: $32.39\"; another user's order or a missing one shows [data-test=\"error\"] \"Error: Order not found\".

contracts.title: 4.1 · Shows the order's products and total
contracts.description: /order.html?id=<number> has a .cart_item per product with .inventory_item_name and .inventory_item_price at the price paid, and [data-test=\"order-total\"] \"Total: $32.39\" for a Backpack order.

contracts.title: 4.2 · Another user's or a missing order is not found
contracts.description: Both show [data-test=\"error\"] \"Error: Order not found\" and nothing of any order.

stories.title: Stock and admin
stories.description: Every product has stock, shown to shoppers and taken off by orders; admin_user sets prices and stock on /admin.html and the shop follows straight away. Package packages/stock-and-admin.

capabilities.title: 1 · Stock and price store
capabilities.description: Each product's stock (10 to start) and admin price in a data file that survives a restart, laid onto browsing's catalog at start and on every change; the browser copy of the catalog is served with the current values.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Every product starts with 10 at its catalog price
contracts.description: With no saved data, each of the six products has stock 10 and its Swag Labs price.

contracts.title: 1.2 · Stock and prices survive a restart
contracts.description: Prices and stock saved before a restart are the ones the shop shows after it.

contracts.title: 1.3 · Taking stock off is all or nothing

contracts.description: [data-test=\"stock\"] reads \"In stock\" from 6 up, \"Only <n> left\" from 5 to 1 and \"Sold out\" at 0, in each .inventory_item and on the product page.

contracts.title: 2.2 · Sold out cannot be added to the cart

contracts.description: /admin.html sends anyone but admin_user to /inventory.html, and the save route refuses anyone but admin_user.

contracts.title: 3.2 · A row per product, saved one at a time

contracts.title: 3.3 · The shop follows the admin straight away
contracts.description: After a save, Products, the product page, the cart, the checkout overview and new orders use the new price and stock; orders already placed keep their prices.

contracts.title: 4.1 · Finishing takes one of each off stock
contracts.description: Each product in a finished order has one less in stock.

contracts.title: 4.2 · A sold-out product stops Finish

stories.title: Reviews
stories.description: Customers who bought a product can review it once with 1 to 5 stars and text; every product shows its reviews and average rating. Package packages/reviews.

capabilities.title: 1 · Review store
capabilities.description: Every review (product, username, stars 1 to 5, text, time) in a data file that survives a restart; at most one per user per product.

contracts.title: 1.1 · Reviews survive a restart
contracts.description: Reviews written before a restart are shown after it.

capabilities.title: 2 · Ratings and reviews shown
capabilities.description: [data-test=\"rating\"] on the product page and each Products item (\"4.5 (2 reviews)\", or \"No reviews yet\"); the product page lists each [data-test=\"review\"] under the product, newest first, with the reviewer's name, 1 to 5 stars and the text.

contracts.title: 3.1 · A customer who bought it can review it once

The owner saw login.spec.ts 'should not be able to login with a locked user' fail 3 of 5 runs in Chrome at line 27 (isErrorMessageDisplayed, which does not wait). The sign-in form posted to the server and the error came back on a new page, so the check raced the navigation. fields.title: Repeated Swag Labs runs will sell the shop out
fields.answer: yes, please add the `npm run reset` command
fields.stakes: Whether Swag Labs' tests keep passing after the shop has been tested a few times, and whether your own tests start from a known state.
fields.context: All new data (accounts, orders, stock, prices, reviews) is kept in files in a data folder and survives restarts, as part two asks. The admin can set stock by hand on /admin.html, but that is six rows to fix before every test run. Order numbers also keep counting up, so a test of yours expecting "Order #1001" only passes on a fresh shop.
fields.options: A) An `npm run reset` command that empties the data folder, so the next start is a fresh shop (stock 10, catalog prices, no orders, accounts or reviews). You run it before a test run. B) The same, but resetting only stock and prices, keeping accounts, orders and reviews. C) Orders by the Swag Labs users (standard_user and friends) take no stock. No command, but your own stock tests must then use a signed-up user. D) Nothing: you restock by hand on /admin.html when needed.
fields.statement: Each product starts with 10 in stock and every finished order takes one off. Swag Labs' checkout specs finish orders on every run, so after about ten runs the Backpack is sold out: its Add to cart is disabled and Finish refuses, and the first list's tests fail. How should the shop get back to a fresh state?
fields.recommendation: A. It is one command, it gives both Swag Labs' tests and yours a known start (stock 10, first order 1001), and it changes no behaviour you asked for. C quietly makes the Swag Labs users special, which your own tests might trip over.

fields.title: Anyone can act as anyone, admin included, by setting the cookie
fields.answer: the cookie is fine as it is for a test shop
fields.stakes: Whether "Another user's order shows Order not found", reviews only by buyers, and an admin-only page mean anything against someone who edits their cookie.
fields.context: This is already true of part one (any username in the cookie counts as signed in). The server will still check who you are on every request, so nothing is protected only by hiding links; the weak point is only that the cookie is believed. Fixing it means the browser keeps one more thing, which part two rules out.
fields.options: A) Accept it: this is a test shop, built to be checked by tests that set the cookie. Build as planned. B) Allow one more cookie: a secret token the server issues at sign-in and checks for signed-up users and admin_user, while Swag Labs users keep working with session-username alone. Changes part 5. C) Something else you have in mind.
fields.statement: The shop knows who you are only from the session-username cookie, which holds the plain username. Your list allows the browser nothing else, and Swag Labs' tests set that cookie by hand, so it cannot be signed. Anyone who sets session-username=admin_user in their browser is the admin, and can see anyone's orders. Is that acceptable for this shop?
fields.recommendation: A, for now. Who is signed in is read in one place (usernameFrom in signing-in's session.js), so B can be added later without touching orders, reviews or admin. Nothing waits on this answer.
